title: Pocket Playlab: SDK quicklaunch protocol & field notes
content:
Purpose
A compact, repeatable protocol for 10–30 minute in-person or virtual "playlab" sessions that get a new integrator from zero to a telemetered sample app using Redwood SDKs. Focus is: low friction, obvious success signals, and data we can use to iterate the docs and starter-kit.

Audience
- New SDK adopters (engineers, SREs, platform integrators)
- Developer advocates running workshops
- Solutions engineers doing customer POC kickoffs

Goals (what counts as success for a single playlab)
- Developer runs sample app end-to-end within 30 minutes and gets a non-empty response from Redwood API.
- Telemetry appears in the console: first_token_latency, request_id, token_cost_estimate.
- Participant can identify next step: embed into minimal app or configure dedicated pool.
- We capture at least 3 qualitative notes per session (pain, confusion, suggestion).

Scope (what this doc covers)
- Pre-lab checklist: env, accounts, creds, dev machine notes.
- 10-min quicklaunch flow (fast path) and 30-min workshop flow (guided path).
- Minimal telemetry assertions and what to look for in Console.
- Quick troubleshooting checklist and common failure modes.
- Post-lab debrief template for advocates to paste into shared tracker.

Unresolved questions (notes to self)
- Should we include an offline emulation mode by default, or point to separate local-mode doc?
- Do we ship a single monolithic starter-app or a microkit with 3 tiny examples (chat, summarize, embed)?

Pre-lab checklist (advocate)
- Account: confirm participant has a Redwood dev API key (instructions + env var snippet).
- Local: node >= 18 or python 3.10; Docker optional.
- Ports: confirm participant can run local server on 3000.
- Tooling: VSCode + recommended extensions (js/py debugger).
- Repo: fork https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter-playlab and checkout branch "pocket-playlab".
- Telemetry: enable demo token-level telemetry in Console (QA org) and confirm access.

10-minute Quicklaunch (fast path)
- 0:00 – welcome, goal, one-line architecture explanation.
- 0:90 – run `npm install` or `pip install -r requirements.txt` in starter folder.
- 3:00 – set env: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-dev-xxxx` + explain scope.
- 4:00 – run sample: `npm run start` (node) or `python app.py`.
- 6:00 – open browser client / curl request, get chat response.
- 8:00 – open Console -> Requests -> filter by owner or request_id; point out token breakdown and latency.
- 9:00 – debrief: what was easy and what blocked you? capture one quick note.

30-minute Workshop (guided path)
- 0–5 min: context + map of paths (chat, embedding search, summarizer).
- 5–12 min: walkthrough of code that constructs a prompt and streams response; demo how to switch model variant.
- 12–20 min: introduce batching and caching flags in sample config; show impact by running synthetic concurrent requests (2–4 workers).
- 20–25 min: quick telemetry dive: show per-route latency and token cost, identify the cold-start pattern in logs.
- 25–30 min: captured next step choices (embed sample into a tiny web app, add feature flag, request dedicated capacity).

Starter repo layout (pocket-playlab) – quick explainer
- /playlab-server (node/python minimal server)
- /playlab-client (tiny web UI demonstrating streaming)
- /scripts/loadtest.sh (toy concurrency script)
- /examples/prompt-sets/*.json (small curated prompts to test regressions)
- README with minimal checklist and debug commands

Minimal commands (copy/paste for workshop)
- Install: `npm ci` or `pip -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt`
- Set key: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-dev-XXXX`
- Start server: `npm run start` or `python playlab-server/app.py`
- Smoke test: `curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/generate -d '{"input":"Hello"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'`
- Loadtest (toy): `bash scripts/loadtest.sh 50 5` -> watch Console for batching effects

Telemetry assertions (what advocates should verify)
- Request shows up in Console within 30s.
- Key fields: request_id (starts with r-), model, first_token_latency_ms, total_tokens_in, total_tokens_out, token_cost_estimate_usd.
- Look for server-side errors (5xx) and client-side retries; record counts.

Common failure modes and quick fixes
- 401 / invalid key: confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, no whitespace, not expired.
- CORS errors on client: use local proxy or run client via `npm run start` which includes proxy.
- Streaming stalled: check network (intermediate proxies) and confirm client uses EventSource / SSE polyfill.
- No telemetry in Console: ensure request uses dev org token and org has telemetry enabled; if not, run with `?debug=1` to print request_id locally.

Advocate debrief template (paste into session tracker)
- Session date: ____
- Participant(s): ____
- Flow used: quicklaunch / workshop
- Success: yes/no (if no, why)
- Telemetry visible: yes/no
- Notable friction (copy/paste): 1) ___ 2) ___ 3) ___
- Suggestions (docs/code): 1) ___ 2) ___

Metrics we want to collect from playlabs
- % successful quicklaunch within 10 minutes
- % see telemetry within 60s of first request
- Top 5 friction points by frequency (freeform)
- Net qualitative score (1–5) from participant post-session rating

Shipping checklist (what to land before we call this ready)
- [ ] starter repo seeded + CI that validates sample runs (GH action).
- [ ] README quicklaunch trimmed to single page with copy/paste commands.
- [ ] telemetry debug flag built-in and toggled off by default.
- [ ] example prompt-set includes a toxic-safety control case to illustrate safety flags.
- [ ] run internal playlab with 5 advocates and collect debriefs.

Follow-ups / tickets (owner suggestions)
- DEVEXP-1423: add `?debug=1` query param that prints request_id on the client (Owner: Jordan).
- SDK-PR-824: add streaming example to TypeScript client (Owner: Theo).
- DOCS-356: simplified quickstart one-pager for sales/demo kits (Owner: Lina).

Notes to the author (Maya)
- Keep this intentionally small and opinionated. The Drive repo will hold many experiments; this doc is the canonical pocket-playlab protocol.
- After 5 internal runs, iterate checklist and remove two least used steps.
- Cross-link back to full onboarding playbook and local-mode emulation doc.

Appendix: sample one-line scripts (for advocates)
- Start everything (dev): `REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-dev-xxxx && npm ci && npm run start`
- Quick curl sample: `curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"input":"Summarize the following: ..."}' http://localhost:3000/generate | jq .`
- How to capture a request_id for debugging: run with `?debug=1` and copy the printed request_id.
__notes: Internal: created to be a compact, high-iteration playbook. Avoid copying existing long-form onramp docs; focus on the micro-experience.
